messages:
rachel: Kicked off an internal loadbench to validate sane defaults for RPM/TPM + burst windows using more realistic client patterns. short tl;dr: 429s started showing up at what we thought were moderate RPMs when many short-lived clients ramp together; p99 latency jumped from ~120ms to ~1.3s. collecting logs and metrics now, sharing repro below. :thinking:

alex: Can you paste the exact test command/profile? Is this single API key hammering or many keys?

rachel: Running multi-key (one per simulated client) to mimic mobile apps. Command we used:
```bash
./loadbench \
  --clients 320 \
  --concurrency 4 \
  --pattern poisson \
  --rps-per-client 0.5 \
  --burst-window 8s \
  --duration 20m \
  --key-scope per-client \
  --payload '{"input":"short prompt"}'
```
Notes: approx 320 clients, each ~30 RPM (0.5 rps), short payloads (~50 tokens output). We intentionally used poisson but no extra jitter on client start times, so many clients hit similar cycles.

sam: Interesting — are caches (prefix/KV) warm? cold cache + many tiny requests can amplify overhead.

rachel: Started cold. We see a cluster of cache misses during the first 3m which coincides with spike. Also noticed spikes line up with the minute boundaries of our synthetic clients (apparently some sync artifact).

anya: Two quick ideas: (1) add randomized client start jitter and inter-request jitter (avoid minute-aligned bursts). (2) try leaky-bucket client smoothing: allow small per-client bursts but smooth refill.

kevin: Also check rate-limiter grouping logic — if per-customer tokens are aggregated at the project level we might be collapsing many per-client requests into the same bucket/window. That causes sudden window exhaustion even though individual clients are low. :point_up:

support-ops: From support side, customers hitting 429s often complain about sudden billing hits when retries multiply. Suggest we track token churn during bursts and add a short-term metric (burst_token_rate) to dashboards.

rachel: Good call. We saw an unexpected billing spike in the test account because retries + short outputs create lots of small calls. Might need to recommend client retry backoff defaults in docs.

alex: Can you repro with these variants and post the minimal diff? I'd like to test: 
- jittered client starts (uniform 0-60s)
- reduce burst-window to 4s and to 12s
- single-key (consolidated) vs multi-key
- pre-warm KV cache vs cold

rachel: Will do. Also adding a run with token-bucket smoothing client-side. Plan to run 4 runs back-to-back and upload logs.

loadbot: loadbench-run-2067890200 finished. summary: 320 clients, peak aggregated RPS ~160, 429s: 8% during minute 2-4, p99 latency 1.28s, median 140ms. raw logs -> gs://redwood-internal/loadbench/2067890200.tar.gz :rocket:

sam: 8% 429s at 160 RPS is concerning. If our production rate limiter has a per-project window of 1s (or coarse windows) that could explain it. Do we have window granularity metrics?

rachel: We're pulling the limiter debug traces now. Preliminary look: many requests hit the same limiter shard and we see bursts of allow/deny churn. Also token refill granularity seems to be per 100ms tranche which may be too coarse for our short bursts.

anya: For experiments: try changing refill granularity to smaller quanta and measure. Also compare token-bucket vs sliding-window counters for fairness across jittery clients.

kevin: FWIW, if we make per-client soft limits + project-level hard cap it might smooth the customer experience while still protecting platform. Eg: per-client token-bucket (small bucket) + project-level leaky bucket.

support-ops: Can we also test the effect of client retries? Add a run with exponential backoff retries enabled in the client vs no retries, that'll show billing and load amplification impact.

rachel: Good point — retry blast is real. I'll run: no-retry, immediate-retry x2, and exp-backoff(100ms->1s) variants.

alex: One more ask — capture per-route queueing time and limiter shard ids in logs. If shard hot-spotting is the issue we can rebalance shard keys or change hashing.

rachel: adding limiter-shard id and route-queue-ms. attaching run plan and ETA. Will post results + graphs in #eng-runtime later today. :white_check_mark:

kevin: If you want, I can run a smaller version on staging with instrumentation turned up (trace sampling 100%) to get stack traces for hot spans.

rachel: That'd be great. I'll share the staging config and the minimal repro. Thanks all.

support-ops: One doc suggestion — create a short KB item: "How to avoid burst-triggered 429s" with recommended client patterns (jitter starts, backoff, avoid sync refreshes). Volunteers? :raising_hand:

anya: I can draft the KB after we finalize the recommended defaults from these runs.

rachel: Perfect — finishing the runs now. Raw logs + perf graphs -> gs://redwood-internal/loadbench/206789/summary-2067890123.html. Follow-up in ~2h.

alex: great, thanks. :thumbsup:
